To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
odorants induce activation of Erk1/2 in granule cells of the olfactory bulb and that odorants enhance survival of newly formed neurons in the olfgang bulb.
odorant exposure in mice activates MAPK in granular cells of the olfactory bulb and that MAPK activation in granular cells promotes the survival of these cells.
odorant-induced activation in the olfactory bulbs of mice promotes the survival of newly generated granule cells, and that this survival depends upon the activation of Erk1/2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of odorants in regulating neuronal survival and differentiation of neurons in the brain.
the role of MAP kinase for the survival of newly generated neurons in the olactory bulb.
the mechanisms that control the survival of newly generated neurons in the olfaction system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
activation of MAP kinase in olfactory bulb neurons promotes survival.
odorant exposure activates MAPK in olatory bulb granule cells, and that this activation is important for survival of newly formed neurons.
activation of MAPk in olfactory bulb neurons by odorants may contribute, in part, to the survival of new neurons in the olfactroy bulb.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
odorants can activate MAPK in the nucleus and in dendrites of granules cells in the olactory bulb.
odorant-induced activation in the olfactory system promotes the survival of olfactory neurons and granule cells in an Erk/MAPK-dependent manner.

activation of MAP kinase (MAPK), a key component in neuronal survival, is induced by some odorants in granule cells of the olfactory bulb and that activation of MAP kinases promotes the survival of these cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
activation of MAP/ERK signaling pathway in the olfactory granule cells promotes survival of newborn granule cells in response to odorants.
odorants can promote survival of granule neurons by activating MAPK.
odorants can activate Erk/MAPK in granule cell dendrites in the olfactory bul, and this activation of Erk/MAPK is important for survival of newly formed neurons in the olfaction system.
